references.text: Ramses is mentioned as one of the store cities that the Israelites built in Egypt, the same place from which they now depart.
Joseph settled his family in the region of Ramses in Egypt, the same place the Israelites are now leaving.
Recounts the departure from Ramses to Sukkot as the first stage of the wilderness journey.
The census in the wilderness shows a similar number of 603,550 men, confirming the count of those who left Egypt.
Moses refers to 600,000 foot soldiers whom he leads, the same number mentioned at the departure from Egypt.
God's promise to Jacob to make his descendants into a great nation in Egypt is now fulfilled at their departure.
God's prophecy to Abraham that his descendants would be strangers in a land and then depart is fulfilled here.
Stephen refers to Moses, who led the people out of Egypt with signs and wonders.
Joseph is mentioned in faith when he prophesied about the Israelites' exodus from Egypt.
Confirms the same event (Ramses to Sukkot) from two different perspectives: the census and the travel account.
Links the departure to Passover and God's act of salvation ('raised hand'), enriching the understanding of the event's significance.
Continues the travel account directly from Sukkot to Etham, confirming the geographical sequence.
Confirms the same journey stage (Sukkot to Etham) and verifies the geography of the exodus.
Identical to [6]; confirms the travel report from Sukkot to Etham.
